title: Remove K Digits
hints: to make a number as small as possible, you generally want smaller digits to appear as far to the left as possible. if a digit is immediately followed by a smaller digit, would you ever want to keep the bigger one?

scan left to right, keeping a stack of digits you've decided to keep so far. while the stack's top digit is bigger than the current digit and you still have removals left, pop it - that's one of your k removals used
after the scan, push the current digit; if you still have removals left over at the end (the digits were non-decreasing), remove them from the very end of the stack instead
finally, strip any leading zeros from the resulting stack, and return '0' if nothing meaningful remains
commonMistakes: forgetting to remove leftover k from the end when the input digits are already non-decreasing
not stripping leading zeros produced after removals
returning an empty string instead of '0' when every digit gets removed

content.problemStatement:
You're given a string `num` representing a non-negative integer, and an
integer `k`.

**Remove exactly `k` digits from `num` so that the digits that remain, kept in their original order, form the smallest possible number.**

The result should not have leading zeros, unless the number itself is "0".
constraints: num consists only of digits and has no leading zeros itself
notes: removing digits creates new leading zeros that must be stripped
k equals num.length, so the entire number is removed (result is 0)
the digits are already in non-decreasing order, so the removals should come from the end

sampleTestCases.explanation: removing the digits 4, 3, and 2 leaves 1, 2, 1, 9 in order
removing the leading 1 leaves 0200, and leading zeros are then dropped, giving 200
removing both digits leaves nothing, but the result must represent a number, so it becomes 0

optimal.pattern: monotonic increasing stack of digits, greedily discarding a larger digit whenever a smaller one follows it

bruteForce.approach: try every combination of k digits to remove, build the resulting string for each, and keep the smallest valid one
bruteForce.time: O(C(n, k) * n) which is exponential
